content: Nelfinavir interacts with various drugs by influencing their metabolism through hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, and other mechanisms such as P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Below are detailed descriptions of these interactions: 1. Erythromycin Base: Nelfinavir increases erythromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction necessitates either avoiding the combination or using an alternative drug. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Erythromycin Ethylsuccinate: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism. Nelfinavir also increases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Close monitoring is required. 3. Erythromycin Lactobionate: Similar to erythromycin ethylsuccinate, this drug increases nelfinavir levels through P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 effects, while nelfinavir increases erythromycin lactobionate levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin Stearate: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 effects, and nelfinavir increases erythromycin stearate levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor closely. 5. Escitalopram: Nelfinavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to increased toxicity and serotonin syndrome. Use caution, monitor closely, and adjust therapy as needed. 6. Eslicarbazepine Acetate: This drug decreases nelfinavir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism but increases nelfinavir levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Esomeprazole: This drug decreases nelfinavir levels through an unspecified mechanism, likely involving CYP2C19 inhibition and reduced gastric absorption. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 8. Estradiol (Oral and Vaginal): Nelfinavir increases estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase estrogen toxicity. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider non-hormonal contraceptives if applicable. 9. Conjugated and Esterified Estrogens: Nelfinavir increases the levels of these estrogens via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution, monitor closely, and consider non-hormonal contraceptives. 10. Eszopiclone: Nelfinavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose of eszopiclone to 1 mg/day, modify therapy, and monitor closely. 11. Ethinyl Estradiol: Nelfinavir increases ethinyl estradiol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially altering estrogen plasma levels and reducing contraceptive efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and consider non-hormonal contraceptives. 12. Ethosuximide: Nelfinavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Etonogestrel: Nelfinavir increases etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Etoposide: Nelfinavir increases etoposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Etravirine: This drug increases nelfinavir levels by decreasing its metabolism, while nelfinavir increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Eucalyptus: Nelfinavir increases eucalyptus levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Everolimus: Nelfinavir increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor closely. 18. Exenatide (Injectable Solution and Suspension): Nelfinavir decreases exenatide effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Famotidine: This drug decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing gastric pH, affecting oral formulations. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Fedratinib: Nelfinavir increases fedratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the fedratinib dose to 200 mg/day and monitor closely. 21. Felbamate: Nelfinavir increases felbamate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor closely. 22. Felodipine: Nelfinavir increases felodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while felodipine increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Fentanyl (Various Forms): Nelfinavir increases fentanyl levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of respiratory depression and sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor patients closely if co-administration is necessary. 24. Fesoterodine: Nelfinavir increases fesoterodine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Fexinidazole: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while nelfinavir decreases fexinidazole levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Finasteride: Nelfinavir increases finasteride levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 27. Finerinone: Nelfinavir increases finerinone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Flibanserin: Nelfinavir increases flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing severe hypotension or syncope. Co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Fluconazole: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Fludrocortisone: Nelfinavir increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Flunisolide (Inhaled): Nelfinavir increases flunisolide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Flurazepam: Nelfinavir increases flurazepam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose, modify therapy, and monitor closely. 33. Fluticasone (Various Forms): Nelfinavir increases fluticasone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing systemic corticosteroid adverse effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for signs of Cushing syndrome. 34. Fluvastatin: Nelfinavir increases fluvastatin toxicity via OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fluvoxamine: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Fosamprenavir: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and nelfinavir increases fosamprenavir levels. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Fosaprepitant: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and nelfinavir increases fosaprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Fosphenytoin: This drug decreases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Fostamatinib: Nelfinavir increases fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and fostamatinib increases nelfinavir levels via P-glycoprotein effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Ganaxolone: Nelfinavir increases ganaxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Garlic: This decreases nelfinavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Gefitinib: Nelfinavir increases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of adverse effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Gepirone: Nelfinavir increases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 44. Gilteritinib: Nelfinavir increases gilteritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for adverse effects if co-administration is unavoidable. 45. Givinostat: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution, monitor ECGs, and withhold treatment if QTc exceeds 500 ms. 46. Glasdegib: Nelfinavir increases glasdegib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for QTc prolongation. 47. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Nelfinavir increases these drug levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Nelfinavir decreases the effects of these drugs, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Grapefruit: This increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Griseofulvin: This decreases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Guanfacine: Nelfinavir increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the guanfacine dose by half for extended-release formulations, and monitor closely. 52. Haloperidol: Nelfinavir increases haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Hydrocodone: Nelfinavir increases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 54. Hydrocortisone: Nelfinavir increases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Nelfinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Ibrutinib: Nelfinavir increases ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration, and interrupt ibrutinib therapy if a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is required. 57. Ibuprofen/Famotidine: This combination decreases nelfinavir levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Idelalisib: Nelfinavir increases idelalisib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for toxicity if co-administration is necessary. 59. Ifosfamide: Nelfinavir decreases ifosfamide levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Iloperidone: Nelfinavir increases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Imatinib: Nelfinavir increases imatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 62. Imipramine: Nelfinavir increases imipramine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Indacaterol (Inhaled): Nelfinavir increases indacaterol levels via P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 modulation. No dose adjustment is required at the 75 mcg dose. 64. Indinavir: Nelfinavir increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Infigratinib: Nelfinavir increases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Insulin (Various Forms): Nelfinavir decreases insulin effects, potentially causing hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 67. Irinotecan (Various Forms): Nelfinavir increases irinotecan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 68. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Nelfinavir increases isavuconazonium levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 69. Isoniazid: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Isradipine: Nelfinavir increases isradipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 71. Istradefylline: This drug increases nelfinavir levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein effects. Use caution and monitor closely. These interactions highlight the importance of careful monitoring, dose adjustments, and alternative therapies when co-administering nelfinavir with other medications.
